import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import re
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.linear_model import RidgeClassifier
from sklearn.calibration import CalibratedClassifierCV
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import log_loss

# Load data
train_df = pd.read_csv("./input/train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv("./input/test.csv")
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("./input/sample_submission.csv")


# Light text preprocessing
def preprocess_text(text):
    text = text.lower()
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text)
    return text.strip()


train_df["text"] = train_df["text"].apply(preprocess_text)
test_df["text"] = test_df["text"].apply(preprocess_text)

# Stratified train/validation split
X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(
    train_df["text"],
    train_df["author"],
    test_size=0.15,
    random_state=42,
    stratify=train_df["author"],
)

# TF-IDF vectorization with expanded n-gram and feature range
tfidf = TfidfVectorizer(
    max_features=8000,
    ngram_range=(1, 3),
    min_df=1,
    max_df=0.95,
    sublinear_tf=True,
    strip_accents="unicode",
)

X_train_tfidf = tfidf.fit_transform(X_train)
X_val_tfidf = tfidf.transform(X_val)
X_test_tfidf = tfidf.transform(test_df["text"])

# Search over alpha values for optimal RidgeClassifier regularization
alpha_values = [0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0]
best_score = float("inf")
best_alpha = None
best_clf = None

for alpha in alpha_values:
    base_clf = RidgeClassifier(alpha=alpha, random_state=42, solver="auto")
    clf = CalibratedClassifierCV(base_clf, method="sigmoid", cv=3)
    clf.fit(X_train_tfidf, y_train)

    val_proba = clf.predict_proba(X_val_tfidf)
    val_score = log_loss(y_val, val_proba)

    if val_score < best_score:
        best_score = val_score
        best_alpha = alpha
        best_clf = clf

print(f"Best alpha: {best_alpha}, Validation Log Loss: {best_score:.6f}")

# Use best classifier for test predictions
test_proba = best_clf.predict_proba(X_test_tfidf)

# Clip probabilities to avoid log(0)
eps = 1e-15
test_proba = np.clip(test_proba, eps, 1 - eps)

# Normalize rows to sum to 1 (required for log loss scoring)
test_proba = test_proba / test_proba.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

# Create submission file
submission = sample_sub.copy()
submission["EAP"] = test_proba[:, 0]
submission["HPL"] = test_proba[:, 1]
submission["MWS"] = test_proba[:, 2]

# Ensure column order matches sample submission
submission = submission[["id", "EAP", "HPL", "MWS"]]

# Save submission
submission.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
